title: Derived tensor evaluation on contractible affine and profinite objects
statement:
Let $T$ be either a w-contractible affine scheme [def-pc-scheme, sk-def-pe-wlocal] with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], or an extremally disconnected profinite set with the site of profinite sets over $T$ and finite jointly surjective covering families. Here profinite means compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected, and extremally disconnected means that closures of open subsets are open. Work in universes [def-weil-size-convention] in which these sites are small relative to their module sheaves. Let $\mathcal O$ be any sheaf of commutative rings, put $A=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O)$, and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and ordinary derived sheaf tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Evaluation $\Gamma(T,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ is exact and preserves all small colimits. Its termwise functor on complexes computes $G=R\Gamma(T,-)$ on every unbounded complex. For all $K,L\in D(\mathcal O)$ the canonical comparison
$$G(K)\otimes_A^L G(L)\longrightarrow G(K\otimes_{\mathcal O}^L L)$$
is an isomorphism, and $A[0]\to G(\mathcal O[0])$ is an isomorphism. These comparisons are natural and compatible with associativity, symmetry and the unit, making $G$ strong symmetric monoidal.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 4.1(1), the w-contractible coherent evaluation and tensor calculation; the same calculation for an arbitrary sheaf of coefficient rings

proof.text: Every covering of $T$ refines a finite disjoint partition. For the affine scheme case apply [det-pe-wcb-clopen-partition] with $X=T$ and its final object $T$. For the profinite case, a covering $\{V_i\to T\}_{i=1}^r$ gives a continuous surjection $\coprod_iV_i\to T$ of compact Hausdorff spaces. By [det-pe-stonean-projective] it has a section $s$. The inverse images $T_i=s^{-1}(V_i)$ are clopen, partition $T$, and their maps to $V_i$ give the required refinement. Empty components can be discarded. Both sites have disjoint finite coproducts stable under pullback, and the component families cover; these statements follow directly from disjoint unions of schemes, respectively profinite spaces, and the covering definitions. Both sites have fibre products, and $T$ (with its identity) is a final object of each. The empty object has the empty covering, and it is strict: an object admitting a map to the empty scheme, respectively the empty profinite set, is itself empty.

source.place: Tag 098H, lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible; Hemo--Richarz--Scholbach Section 3, definition of the profinite site

proof.text: Both sites satisfy the disjoint-coproduct hypotheses, including the strict empty object, by step 1. Apply [lem-zl-partition-module-evaluation-localization] at $W=T$: evaluation is exact and preserves all small colimits, and its termwise localization computes $G=R\Gamma(T,-)$ with the stated unit.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), exact coherent evaluation; Stacks Tags 0F63 (proetale.tex, lemma-presheaf-value-weakly-contractible), 03DA (sites-modules.tex, lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), 079P (injectives.tex, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck); arbitrary ring-sheaf extension of the argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-partition-section-tensor-flat] at the final object $W=T$ of step 1, with the exact evaluation just obtained. The actual ordinary section tensor pairing is invertible and coherent, and evaluation sends flat sheaves to flat $A$-modules. The finite-relation lifting assertion includes the zero relation and zero coefficients.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), section tensor calculation; Stacks Tags 03EK (sites-modules.tex, section-tensor-product), 00HK (algebra.tex, lemma-flat-eq); arbitrary ring-sheaf and partition-site formulation

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-evaluation-adapted-flat-telescope] to this exact, cocontinuous, flat-preserving evaluation. Every unbounded complex has a flat-term K-flat telescope resolution whose evaluation is K-flat over $A$ and remains a resolution. Thus these are adapted representatives for both factors of any derived tensor.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), unbounded computation expanded by the compatible flat tower and telescope; Stacks Tags 077J (sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-resolution-by-direct-sums-extensions-by-zero) and 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), together with the same construction after evaluation

proof.text: Use [lem-zl-derived-section-pairing-coherence] with these adapted resolutions and the ordinary section pairings. Its normalized natural comparison is exactly the canonical map in the statement, including the derived-to-ordinary comparison on arbitrary flat-term K-flat representatives. It is invertible on the adapted representatives and hence for every $K,L$. The same lemma supplies associativity, signed symmetry, both unit diagrams and the identity on $A[0]$, so $G$ is strong symmetric monoidal.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1), canonical tensor comparison, unbounded computation and coherence; Stacks Tags 06YU (sites-cohomology.tex, definition-derived-tor) and 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived); adapted-resolution formulation without preservation of every K-flat complex

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.1(1): finite-partition sheafification argument expanded for arbitrary ring sheaves; unbounded comparison proved using the flat-resolution telescope of Stacks Tags 077J and 06YS.
